title: SME homepage: the Society for Mining, Metallurgy and Exploration landing page
answer: This is the homepage of the Society for Mining, Metallurgy and Exploration, a professional society for mining and metallurgical engineers. It is a landing page, not a research document. The most useful thing it states is that SME describes itself as a world leader in information sharing and networking for engineering professionals in mining and metallurgy, and that it is a member society of OneMine, the SME Foundation and AIME. It contains no technical content on AI, machine learning or automation.

sections.body: The Society for Mining, Metallurgy and Exploration publishes this page as its own homepage. It is a single landing page rather than a report, article or technical paper, and the harvested text consists of a short self-description, a copyright line and a list of affiliations. The only date stated is the copyright notice, 2026. The page names SME as a member society of OneMine, the SME Foundation and the American Institute of Mining, Metallurgical, and Petroleum Engineers, known as AIME. No author, publication date, methodology or subject scope is given beyond the society's own description of its field.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page says that the Society for Mining, Metallurgy and Exploration is a world leader in information sharing and networking for engineering related professionals in the mining and metallurgical fields. That sentence is repeated, and it is the whole of the substantive content. The rest of the harvested text is a copyright line and a note that SME is a member society of OneMine, the SME Foundation and the American Institute of Mining, Metallurgical, and Petroleum Engineers, or AIME. There is no discussion of artificial intelligence, machine learning or automation anywhere in the supplied text. There is no description of working groups, committees, publications, conferences or research programmes. There are no findings, no case studies, no data and no named authors. A reader arriving at this page would learn what SME is and which organisations it belongs to, and nothing about its technical output. Any claim that SME publishes working-group research on AI, machine learning and automation in mineral processing is not supported by this text. The page is a front door to a membership organisation, and the substance behind it sits on other pages that were not harvested here.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The text gives no figures. The only date is the copyright notice, 2026 SME All Rights Reserved. The claims it makes are that SME is a world leader in information sharing and networking for engineering related professionals in mining and metallurgy, and that SME is a member society of OneMine, the SME Foundation and the American Institute of Mining, Metallurgical, and Petroleum Engineers (AIME). No numbers, definitions or technical positions appear.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in mining would use this page only as a signpost. It identifies SME as a professional society for mining and metallurgical engineers and shows that it belongs to OneMine, a shared mining library, and to AIME. Those affiliations suggest where technical material might be found, but this page does not contain any. It cannot be cited as evidence that SME publishes working-group research on AI, machine learning and automation in mineral processing, because the harvested text says nothing of the kind. Anyone wanting to support that point would need to cite a specific SME publication, committee page or paper rather than the homepage.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Mining

sections.body: The source is a homepage and is thin. It does not cover AI, machine learning, automation, mineral processing, research programmes, publications or events. It names no authors and gives no publication date beyond the 2026 copyright line. It is promotional in tone, describing SME as a world leader, and it is partial in the sense that the harvested text is a small fragment of a larger site. It is not a commercial product page, but it is a membership organisation's front page, so its purpose is to introduce the society rather than to present findings. Nothing here can be verified beyond the society's own self-description.
